newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher after USDA trims end stocks.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher after USDA trims end stocks.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher after the USDA trimmed its estimate for 1996-97 wheat ending stocks, and traders said strength in CBOT corn and beans helped wheat extend its gains.
Wheat opened higher after USDA, in its November crop report, pegged wheat ending stocks at 435 million bushels. That marked a sharp decrease from its previous estimate of 470 million bushels.
Traders said bull-spreading helped the December contract advance to $4.30 per bushel. Dec traded as high as $4.35 when buy stops were hit at $4.30.
KCBT wheat closed 3-1/2 to 10 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up nine cents at $4.32-1/2. It was the fifth consecutive higher close for KCBT December wheat.
Traders said the Dec/March spread traded as wide as 32-1/2 cents per bushel. It traded late Monday at 31 cents.

Commission houses were key featured players Tuesday. CIS sold three million March bushels and also bull-spread one million Dec/March bushels between 30 and 32-1/2 cents, traders said. Also, Benson-Quinn bought 2.3 million Dec bushels, traders said, while Prudential and FIMAT each bear-spread two million March/Dec bushels between 29 and 32 cents.
